summary: Philip Kapleau was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki, Hakuun Ryoko Yasutani, Soen Nakagawa, and Sogaku Harada. He founded the Rochester Zen Center and the Chapin Mill Retreat Center (1996).

Philip L. Quinn (1940–2004) was a philosopher and religious studies scholar. Educated at Georgetown, Delaware, and Pittsburgh, he taught at Brown (~1974–1985), became John A. O'Brien Professor at Notre Dame (1985), and served as APA President (1994–1995).

Philip Lutgendorf is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who earned his B.A. at the University of Chicago (~1968–1987). He joined the University of Iowa in 1985 and served as President of the American Institute of Indian Studies (2010–2018).

Philip Novak works in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of Notre Dame and Syracuse University, he joined the faculty at Dominican University of California as a teacher around 1980.

Philip Stanley Rawson (1924–1995) was an art historian and Indologist educated at Winchester College, Oxford, the Courtauld Institute, and SOAS. He taught at the Royal College of Art and served as Dean at the University of London (~1981–1984).

Philip Whalen (1923–2002) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies figure who studied at Reed College and under Richard Baker. He served as head monk at Dharma Sangha (1984) and abbot of Hartford Street Zen Center (1991).

Philipp André Maas is an Indologist and philosopher who earned his doctorate at Bonn (1997–2004) under Vogel and Wezler. He has held positions at Vienna, Leipzig (2016–2026), Halle-Wittenberg (2021–2022), and Munich (2024).

Philipp Keiper (1855–1927) was a linguist and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He completed his PhD at Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1873–1877) under Friedrich von Spiegel, later teaching at secondary schools in Erlangen, Ludwigshafen, and Zweibrücken (1890).
Philipp Schäffer (1894–1943) was a scholar in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He earned his Ph.D. at Heidelberg University (1920–1924) studying under Max Walleser.

Philippe Colinet (1853–1917) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Ghent, KU Leuven, Berlin, and Paris. A student of Harlez, Schmidt, Bréal, and Bergaigne, he became an extraordinary professor (1887) and ordinary professor (1889) at KU Leuven.

Philippe Stern (1895–1979) was an art historian and Indologist who studied under Louis Finot. He served as a professor at École du Louvre (1929–1965) and as Conservateur-en-chef at the Guimet Museum (1954–1965).

Philippe Turenne specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and earned a PhD from McGill University (attested 2010), supervised by G. Victor Sōgen Hori.

Philippe Édouard Foucaux (1811–1894) was an Indologist and Tibetologist who studied under Eugène Burnouf. He held professorships at INALCO (from 1842), the Collège de France (from 1857), and the University of Paris (~1862–1894).
Phillip Bloom is a scholar of art history, archaeology, and Sinology. He earned his PhD at Harvard University under the supervision of Eugene Y. Wang, Yukio Lippit, and James Robson.

Philoxène Luzzatto (1829–1854) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Samuel David Luzzatto. He was a member of the Accademia Galileiana and the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft (~1851–1854).
Phong Tran is a scholar in Indology and archaeology. He held posts at Leiden University (attested 2020) and the Library of Congress (attested 2023).
Phra Athiwat Thammawatsiri is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Ph.D. in Buddhist Studies from Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University, where he also serves as a lecturer and researcher.

Phra Brahmapundit (born 1955) works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He served as Rector of Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (~1997–2018), Chief Abbot of Wat Prayurawongsawat (~2004), and President of both the ICDV (~2004) and the IABU (~2007).

Phra Rajavaramuni is a Buddhist studies scholar educated at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University and Sukhothai Thammathirat Open University. As of 2012, he was Dean of the Faculty of Buddhist Studies and Deputy Vice Rector at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University.

Phra Sigambhirayan is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Bachelor of Liberal Arts at Sukhothai Thammathirat Open University and an M.A. in Buddhist Studies at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University.
